challenge: Logging what you did is useful and tedious, so nobody keeps it up. Every tracker wants a form, a category and a date for each entry.

The bet: if logging were one gesture — hold, talk, let go — people would do it. That means turning an unstructured ramble into clean, correctly dated entries, cheaply enough to run on free model tiers.
architectureCaption: A capture goes to the cheapest tier that can handle it correctly; validation, dates and the confidence gate always run in code.

steps.title: Capture
steps.desc: Hold to talk. The phone uses Web Speech or sends audio to Whisper; the dev server issues its own certificate so the mic works over the LAN.

steps.title: Guard
steps.desc: Whisper invents text on silence — repetition loops or an echoed prompt — so decoder statistics and a prompt-echo check drop it before it becomes 'activity'.

steps.title: Cache first
steps.desc: Clauses are normalised (fillers stripped, tense kept) and matched against learned patterns with {n} slots; fully known captures cost 0 tokens.

steps.title: One structured call
steps.desc: Only unknown clauses go to gpt-oss-120b in a single call with low reasoning effort.

steps.title: Validate and file
steps.desc: Dedup, date resolution, todo closing and the confidence gate run in code; a question is asked only when a wrong guess would corrupt the log.

sceneCaptions: One ramble split into an activity, a spend and a closed todo.
Measured: an agent loop vs one structured call vs a cached repeat.
Under the hood: capture, guard, cache, one call.

decisions.title: One call beats an agent loop
decisions.desc: On the same 95-word capture, a 14-call tool loop spent 49,054 tokens in ~17 s and missed an activity; one structured call covered all 12 in ~1 s for ~1,000 tokens. Bounded extraction has nothing to explore.

decisions.title: The cache is the moat
decisions.desc: Every resolved clause is learned, keyed by a signature with numbers as slots — so repeats are free and the cache becomes personal, which competitors can't copy.

decisions.title: Conservative caching
decisions.desc: A wrong cached entry is silent and repeats, so todos, dated clauses, low-confidence items and clauses that lean on a neighbour are never cached.

decisions.title: Nothing logged that wasn't said
decisions.desc: Logging a Whisper hallucination is worse than logging nothing, so transcripts are gated on the decoder's own statistics before anything is filed.

roadmap: Test Whisper properly on the user's own accent and vocabulary — the one risk that gates the native build.
Ship as a PWA and measure whether people keep talking to it after week three.
Capture surfaces on Android: the notification bar is shipped; a Quick Settings tile and home-screen widget are written and waiting on a build.
